added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own arm records, each of which ran to a summary line and a bare final EXIT= line. baseline_suite: revision 977adcbef6fbd4cfc3a2a3d59a694f9c37407902, completed true, exit_status 0, failure_count 0, failure_ids [], log logs/baseline.log, summary '58 passed in 34.48s'. after_suite: revision f9cba3c0ee36023fe85d68e652be85b8c5efac31, completed true, exit_status 0, failure_count 0, failure_ids [], log logs/after.log, summary '61 passed in 33.77s'. Neither arm names a failing test id, so after-minus-base over test ids is empty and the added count is zero.

findings.text: blocking: the reuse replaces _WAIT_LIVE_PROBE_STATES (ten tokens: running, pending, queued, waiting, completing, configuring, requeued, resizing, signaling, suspended) with _WAIT_LIVE_STATE_TOKENS from reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:1068 (running, pending, waiting only), so a probe reporting any of the other seven loses its live reading, _wait_probe_reported_limit returns None at :1215, and the wait is judged by the 900 s default. That is the misreading s7 exists to fix, re-admitted for a scheduler-state probe; the owner that would have preserved the behaviour is _JOB_LIVE_STATES at reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:54. No test covers those spellings and gate/after.log passes 61 at EXIT=0 without noticing.

blocking: negative_control_log names .../logs/negative-control.log, which does not exist - logs/ holds only baseline.log and after.log - while the checkpoint (line 6) and negative_control_note (line 15) claim three finding replays there. The only control run on disk is gate/negative-control.log, which replays one case and ends EXIT=1. Promotion reads the control's facts from the named path, so the field names nothing a reader can open.

blocking: the tests line is not the literal text a shell was handed - it carries a stray double quote and a Python replace expression, and a duplicated test-file operand after it - so a promotion that fills its gate receipt from this line cannot re-run it. The baseline_suite and after_suite blocks name their commands correctly, so the arm evidence survives; the field the contract reads for the gate receipt does not.

non-blocking: _wait_probe_answered is added to a file the node was not fenced to write - prompt.txt:84-91 grants recovery_liveness.py, recovery_classification.py, recovery_watch.py, the new test and the fragment, and names no recovery_wait.py. The placement is the one the plan's s7 write paths name for the probe readings and is the right owner, so this is a fence breach rather than a design error; the alternative, leaving the helper in recovery_liveness.py, is the fork this commit was repairing.

non-blocking: artifacts, evidence_inputs and outside_scope still read the literal template tokens ARTIFACTS, EVIDENCE and OUTSIDE after the repair round whose blocking finding was exactly this class of unfilled field. The arm records were restored, so promotion reads its suite pair; a reader looking for the run's headline metrics or for the tests recorded in outside_scope finds a token instead.

non-blocking: this commit deletes the _watch_snapshot(...)["state"] == "waiting" assertion from the live-job case, which passed at its parent (the 60-passed arm at 4265b8669e ran it), without recording the removal in the commit body that does record the probe-echo removal. The row-level classification assertions at lines 193-194 still read the case, so the surface is partially covered and the node does not hold on it.

justifications.durability: gate/negative-control.log reddens tests/test_a_declared_wait_is_judged_against_itself.py:191 with 'assert True is False' at EXIT=1 when the reported limit is not read, but no case covers the seven live-state spellings this commit dropped.
justifications.evidence: logs/baseline.log and logs/after.log are complete and reconcile with the fragment's 61, but the done_when's fourth clause has no log naming this head and manifest.md:12 is not a command a shell ran.
justifications.fit: the moved helper follows the module's docstring-stating-the-mechanism idiom and the corrected comment at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1591-1599 now describes the reading its code implements.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1128 reads the live state from a three-token set, so a probe reporting 'COMPLETING 04:00:00', live and limit-bearing at this commit's parent, is judged against the 900 s default and reads wait-aged.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:914 and reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:526 are extended rather than copied, but recovery_liveness.py:1128 reuses a three-token vocabulary where reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:54 owns the wider scheduler-live set, so the change narrows a capability instead of extending its owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 4265b8669e..f9cba3c0ee includes reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py, which the dispatch fence at prompt.txt:84-91 does not grant.
